name: Saint Anthony of Padua
history: A Portuguese canon who became a Franciscan, hoping for martyrdom in Morocco, and instead became the most famous preacher of his age. He taught theology to the friars at Saint Francis’s request and preached across Italy and France. He died at thirty-six and was canonised within a year. He is a Doctor of the Church and the patron of lost things.
life: Fernando Martins was born in Lisbon and joined the Augustinian canons, studying Scripture deeply at Coimbra. In 1220 the bodies of five Franciscans martyred in Morocco were brought there, and he resolved to follow them, taking the name Anthony. He reached Morocco but fell ill, and the ship bringing him home was driven to Sicily. Unknown and unregarded, he served in a hermitage until, at an ordination at Forlì, he was asked to preach without preparation and astonished everyone. Francis wrote to him as ‘my bishop’ and asked him to teach the brothers theology, so long as study did not quench the spirit of prayer. He preached against heresy and usury, and crowds too large for churches gathered in fields to hear him. Worn out, he died near Padua on 13 June 1231. Pius XII declared him a Doctor in 1946.
prayerTo: Saint Anthony, preacher of the Gospel and friend of the poor, you knew the Scriptures by heart and loved Christ in them. Help me to find what I have lost, and above all to find again any grace I have let slip. Pray for the poor, and teach me to give to them freely. Amen.
penance: Give alms today for the poor, in the old custom of Saint Anthony’s Bread, perhaps the cost of a meal.
meditation: Anthony said that actions speak louder than words, and urged preachers to let their words teach and their deeds speak. Which of your words is still waiting for its deed?
